# OpenTempl: full text

> OpenTempl is a free, open source (MIT) design app for posters, social media posts and slides, with 337 templates, that works offline and needs no account.

This file holds the text of every page on opentempl.org except the individual prompt pages, which are summarised. Updated November 2026.

---

# Canva alternative with no account or login

URL: https://opentempl.org/canva-alternative-no-account
Updated: 2026-11-02

Design without making an account

Open OpenTempl and start. There is nothing to sign up for, no email to give and no login to remember. Your designs are saved on your device. It is not affiliated with Canva.

 What no account means 
 There is no OpenTempl account. The app does not know who you are, so it has no profile to keep, no sign in screen and no trial that ends. Starting a live session with someone works from a link, not from accounts. 
 When this matters 
  School and work computers where signing up is blocked.  Kids and classrooms, where nobody should hand an email address to a design tool.  Quick jobs: a poster for tonight, a menu for tomorrow.  People who would rather not be in yet another database.  
 The trade offs 
 No account also means no cloud. Your designs live on the device where you made them. 
  Nothing syncs between your phone, laptop and desktop.  In the web version, clearing your browser data removes your designs. Export the OpenTempl file for anything you want to keep.  To work on another computer, move the file.  If you want to share a design with someone else live, start a session and send the link. It runs directly between browsers and is encrypted with a key in the link.  
 Back up your work 
 Export an OpenTempl file from the File menu. It holds the whole design, with its pictures and video clips, and opens on any computer with OpenTempl. Version history keeps a snapshot every ten minutes inside the app. 
 What does need a key 
 The Generate tab makes images with your own OpenAI key. The key stays on your device. That is the one place an account exists, and it is yours with OpenAI, not with OpenTempl.   Open the editor  

Is my data collected?
There is no OpenTempl account, and no OpenTempl server stores your designs. Fonts load from Google Fonts. The facts page lists exactly what needs a connection.

Can I collaborate without accounts?
Yes. Start a live session and send the link. Both people edit at once, and each sees the other's cursor.

How do I move designs to another computer?
Export the OpenTempl file, copy it over, and open it there.

---

# Canva alternative that works offline | OpenTempl

URL: https://opentempl.org/canva-alternative-offline
Updated: 2026-11-02

A Canva alternative that works without internet

OpenTempl is a design app that loads once and then works without a connection. You can create a new poster, post or slide deck, edit it and export it, all offline. It is free, open source and has no account to sign in to. It is not affiliated with Canva.

 How it works 
 The editor runs on your device, and your designs are saved there while you work. After the first load, the app is kept for offline use. Chrome and Edge may offer to install it as an app, so it starts like any other. The desktop builds for Mac, Windows and Linux carry the whole editor with them. 
 Any design can also be saved as an OpenTempl file, an editable file you can copy, back up and email. The export formats are PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG, PDF, PowerPoint, MP4 and GIF, and none of them need a connection. 
 Canva and offline 
 Canva has an offline editing feature. Its help centre says the desktop app and Android support it, and iOS does not. You mark designs as available offline while you are connected, then edit them offline. You can edit existing designs only, not create new ones. Videos show as still images and uploads need a connection. Canva's help pages give 14 days in one article and 7 days in others as the time you can stay offline before you reconnect. 
 So the difference is simple. In Canva you prepare for offline. In OpenTempl, offline is how the app works. The Canva details come from its help centre as read in October 2026; check the current pages, because they change. 
 What still needs a connection 
 Be ready for these: 
  The first load, and updates.  Fonts you have not used before. OpenTempl offers 1,344 Google Fonts and fetches each one the first time you use it, then keeps it. Fonts you have used stay available offline. Your own font files always work.  Searching icons and stock photos, which come from online libraries.  Background removal the first time. The app downloads a small model once, then removal runs on your computer.  Live sessions with other people.  The Generate tab, which calls OpenAI with your own key.  
 Everything else works without a network. 
 Where offline matters 
 A teacher making handouts on a train. A cafe owner with weak wifi who needs tomorrow's menu printed. A student on a school computer that blocks sign ups. Anyone who wants a design to stay on their computer until they decide to share it. 
 What you give up 
 OpenTempl does not sync designs between devices. If you work on two computers, move the file yourself. The web version stores designs in your browser, so clearing your browser data removes them; export an OpenTempl file for anything you care about. The desktop app is the safer home for your work.   Open the editor  

Can I create a new design offline?
Yes. Once the app has loaded, you can start a new design from any template with no connection.

Do fonts work offline?
Fonts you have already used do. A font you have never used needs one online load first. Fonts you add from your own files always work.

Where are my files stored?
On your device, in the app's storage and in any OpenTempl file you save. No OpenTempl server holds them.

Does it sync between devices?
No. Copy the file to move a design.

Is Canva available offline?
Partly. Canva can edit designs you chose in advance while offline, for a limited time. See the section above.

---

# Canva alternative: free, open source, works offline

URL: https://opentempl.org/canva-alternative
Updated: 2026-11-02

A Canva alternative you can keep, offline and free

OpenTempl is a free, open source design app for posters, social posts, slides, menus and invitations. It works offline, needs no account and has no paid tier. It is not affiliated with Canva.

 If you are looking for a Canva alternative, the useful question is what you use Canva for. For making your own posters, posts and slides, OpenTempl does the job and you keep the files. For team workspaces, huge stock libraries and phone apps, it does not, and Canva is the better tool. 
 Who should switch 
 Switch if you: 
  make posters, Instagram posts, flyers, menus or slides for yourself, a small business, a club or a class  want to open the app without logging in  work on a train, in a classroom with poor wifi or on a computer that blocks sign ups  want transparent PNG, SVG or print PDF without paying  would rather have a file you own than a design stored in someone else's account  like templates with a strong visual style, not only the clean corporate kind  
 Stay with Canva if you: 
  share folders and brand approvals with a team  need millions of stock photos, videos and music tracks  design mostly on your phone  rely on Canva's AI writing or scheduling tools  
 What you get 
   Templates.  337 across 34 styles, from Swiss grid and riso zine to brutalist, Bauhaus and Y2K.  Browse them .   A real editor.  Pages, smart guides that show the spacing, 23 shapes, a vector pen, charts, tables, QR codes, curved text, 1,344 Google Fonts and your own font files.   Photo tools.  Crop, masks, filters, adjustment sliders and background removal that runs on your computer.   Resize and repeat.  Magic resize into any format, bulk create from a pasted table, brand kits.   Import.  PowerPoint and PDF files, with editable text.   Export.  PNG including transparent, JPG, WebP, SVG, PDF for screen or print, PowerPoint, MP4 and GIF.   Live editing.  Share a link and edit together, with each other's cursors and selections.   Images from your own OpenAI key.  32 styles in the Generate tab. OpenAI bills you.  
 OpenTempl next to other Canva alternatives 
       OpenTempl  Penpot  Polotno Studio  Inkscape  Canva      Open source  Yes, MIT  Yes, MPL 2.0  No, the SDK is a commercial product  Yes, GPL  No    Works offline  Yes  Only if you self host  Not claimed  Yes  Limited, see below    Account needed  No  Yes, or self host  No  No  Yes    Built around templates  Yes  No, it is a design and prototyping tool  Yes  No, it is a vector editor  Yes    Price  Free  Free, with paid team plans  Studio is free, the SDK is paid  Free  Free plan and paid plans     
 Sources: Penpot's comparison page and media kit, Polotno's Canva alternative page, Canva's help centre, read in November 2026. Plans and licences change, so check each project before you decide. 
 Is it better than Canva? 
 It depends on the job. OpenTempl is better in these ways: 
  It works offline from the first minute and creates new designs offline. Canva's offline mode edits designs you marked ahead of time, for a limited period.  You do not need an account.  The files are yours, in an editable OpenTempl file and in open formats.  Exports that Canva keeps behind a paid plan, such as transparent PNG and SVG, are free. See  Canva Pro features in OpenTempl .  It is open source.  
 Canva is better in these ways: 
  The template and stock library is far larger.  It has phone apps.  It has team workspaces, comments, approvals and brand controls at company scale.  It has AI tools and a content planner built in.  It has years of polish and a very large user base. OpenTempl is at version 0.1.  
 Moving your Canva work over 
 In Canva, download a design as PDF or PowerPoint. Open the file in OpenTempl. PowerPoint files keep their text, shapes, pictures and notes. PDF text becomes editable text boxes. Fonts that are not available get a close match, and complex effects can flatten, so check the result before you rely on it. There is no direct Canva import.   Open the editor  

Is OpenTempl a Canva clone?
No. It is a separate editor written from scratch, with its own templates and its own look. It does not use Canva's code, content or servers.

Is OpenTempl better than Canva?
For working offline, owning your files and exporting without a paid plan, yes. For templates and stock at scale, phone apps and team features, no. The lists above give both sides.

Can I import Canva designs?
Download the design from Canva as PDF or PowerPoint and open that file in OpenTempl. There is no direct Canva import.

Is there a catch?
It is a young project by one maker. There is no cloud sync and no phone app, and the desktop installers are not code signed yet. The Generate tab uses your own OpenAI account, which costs money for each image.

Which Canva Pro features are free in OpenTempl?
Background removal, magic resize, brand kits, bulk create, transparent PNG, SVG export, print PDF with bleed, version history and custom fonts. See the list.

---

# Canva Pro features for free: what OpenTempl includes

URL: https://opentempl.org/canva-pro-free
Updated: 2026-11-02

Canva Pro features you get free in OpenTempl

Canva keeps several of its most used tools on paid plans. OpenTempl includes an equivalent of each one for free, with no trial and no sign in. OpenTempl is a separate app written from scratch. It does not use or unlock anything from Canva, and it is not affiliated with Canva.

 The list 
 The Canva column reflects Canva's own help and pricing pages as read in October 2026. Plans change, so check canva.com/pricing for today's terms. 
     Feature  On Canva  In OpenTempl      Transparent background PNG  Paid plan  Free, up to 4x size    SVG export  Paid plan  Free    Print PDF with bleed and crop marks  Paid plan  Free    Custom fonts  Paid plan to upload  Free. Add any font file, plus 1,344 Google Fonts    Brand kit  One kit with three colours on the free plan, more on paid plans  Free. Logos, colours and fonts    Version history  Paid plan  Free. A snapshot every ten minutes    Background remover  Paid plan  Free, runs on your computer    Magic resize  Paid plan  Free    Bulk create  Paid plan, with row limits  Free     
 How each one works 
  Background removal.  Select a photo and press Remove background. The cut out runs in the app with an open model (BiRefNet lite, MIT licence), so your photo is not uploaded for it. The first use downloads the model once. 
  Magic resize.  Choose a format, such as a story, a poster or a slide, and OpenTempl lays the design out again. Do it in place or keep a copy. 
  Brand kit.  Save your logos, colours and fonts once and apply them to any design. 
  Bulk create.  Paste rows from a spreadsheet and get one page for each row. Good for name badges, product cards and menus. 
  Version history.  The app saves a snapshot every ten minutes. Go back to one when you break something. 
  Print PDF.  Choose print, set the bleed and get crop marks. OpenTempl does not do CMYK colour or ICC profiles yet, so if your print shop needs CMYK, convert the PDF in a prepress tool. 
 What Canva Pro has that OpenTempl does not 
  A far larger library of premium templates, photos, video and music.  Phone apps.  AI writing, image editing and design tools built in. OpenTempl has only the Generate tab, which uses your own OpenAI key and costs money for each image.  Team workspaces, approvals and brand controls at company scale.  Content scheduling and publishing to social networks.  CMYK colour for print.    Open the editor  

Is OpenTempl a hacked or cracked version of Canva Pro?
No. It does not use Canva's code, servers or content. It is a separate open source app.

Do I need a Canva account to use OpenTempl?
No, and you do not need an OpenTempl account either.

Can students and teachers use it free?
Everyone uses it free. There are no tiers.

Will these features become paid later?
The code is MIT licensed, so the version you have stays free and open whatever happens next.

# Canva vs OpenTempl: an honest comparison

URL: https://opentempl.org/canva-vs-opentempl
Updated: 2026-11-02

Canva vs OpenTempl

Canva is the large, polished default for design on the web. OpenTempl is a small, free, open source app that works offline. This page sets them side by side, including where Canva is better. OpenTempl is not affiliated with Canva. The Canva details come from its help and pricing pages as read in October 2026; check canva.com for today's terms.

 Side by side 
       Canva  OpenTempl      Price  Free plan, paid plans for more tools and exports  Free, no paid plan    Licence  Proprietary  MIT, open source    Account  Needed  Not needed    Works offline  Edit designs you marked in advance, for a limited time  Yes, and new designs too    Where your files live  In your Canva account  On your device, plus an editable file you keep    Templates  A very large library  337 in 34 styles    Stock photos, video, music  Very large library, some behind a paid plan  Built in photos and objects, plus Openverse and Iconify search    Transparent PNG, SVG, print PDF  Paid plan  Free    Background remover, magic resize, bulk create  Paid plan  Free    AI tools  Built in, metered  Optional Generate tab with your own OpenAI key    Import  Several formats  PowerPoint and PDF, with editable text    Real time editing with others  Yes, with accounts and team features  Yes, from a link, peer to peer    Team features  Workspaces, approvals, brand controls  None    Phone apps  Yes  No    Publishing and scheduling  Yes  No    CMYK for print  On paid plans  Not yet     
 Pick Canva if 
  You work in a team that shares folders, comments and approvals.  You need a huge stock library, or video and music tracks.  You make designs on your phone.  You want built in AI writing and a content planner.  You want the most polished, most documented tool, with years behind it.  
 Pick OpenTempl if 
  You want to open an app and start, with no account.  You work offline, or on a computer that blocks sign ups.  You want transparent PNG, SVG and print PDF without a plan.  You want files you own, in a format you can keep and open source code behind it.  You like templates with a clear visual style: Swiss grid, riso, brutalist, Bauhaus, Y2K.  
 What each does better 
 Canva is better at scale: more templates, more stock, more people, more tools around the editor. OpenTempl is better at independence: it runs without a network, without an account and without a paid plan, and the exports are not held back. For one person making a poster, a post or a deck, that can be the whole decision. For a company with brand rules and ten people editing the same files, it cannot. 
 See also:  Canva alternatives compared ,  the offline question  and  Canva Pro features in OpenTempl .   Open the editor  

Is OpenTempl better than Canva?
For working offline, keeping your files and exporting without a paid plan, yes. For templates, stock, phone apps and teams, Canva is better.

Can I move from Canva?
Download a design from Canva as PDF or PowerPoint and open it in OpenTempl. Check the result, because fonts and effects may change. There is no direct import.

Does OpenTempl have Canva's templates?
No. It has its own 337 templates, made for OpenTempl.

Does OpenTempl copy Canva?
No. It is a separate editor written from scratch.

# Free Canva alternative with no watermark or paywall

URL: https://opentempl.org/free-canva-alternative
Updated: 2026-11-02

A free Canva alternative with nothing held back

OpenTempl is free in the plain sense: no trial, no watermark, no locked exports and no account. The licence is MIT. It is not affiliated with Canva.

 What free means here 
  No paid plan, now or inside the app. There is nothing to unlock.  No watermark on anything you export.  No ads and no sign up.  The one thing that costs money is optional. If you use the Generate tab, you paste your own OpenAI key and OpenAI bills you for the images. Skip it and you pay nothing.  
 Exports you do not pay for 
 PNG, with a transparent background and up to 4x size. JPG and WebP. SVG. PDF for screen, or for print with bleed and crop marks. PowerPoint with editable text. MP4 video of your pages and animations. GIF. A ZIP of all pages. The editable OpenTempl file. 
 How a free project pays for itself 
 OpenTempl is a project by one person, Noah, and there is no paid plan behind it. The MIT licence means the version you download stays free and open even if the project changes direction. 
 Free options compared 
 Canva has a free plan, and it is generous. It also has paid plans that add some exports and tools, and it needs an account. Browser tools such as Polotno Studio are free and need no sign up, but they run online. Desktop editors such as Inkscape and GIMP are free and open source, but they are not built around templates. OpenTempl sits between them: templates and a simple editor, installed and offline, free and open. 
  See how it compares in detail , or  read about the Canva Pro features it includes . 
 Limits 
 There are no team workspaces, no phone app and 337 templates, not millions. The desktop installers are not code signed yet.   Open the editor  

Is there a watermark?
No.

Is there a free trial that ends?
No. There is no paid plan to end up on.

Will it become paid?
The code is MIT licensed, so the version you have stays free and open whatever happens next.

Is it safe to use?
It runs in your browser or as a desktop app, and your designs stay on your device. The desktop installers are unsigned for now, so your system will ask you to confirm the first launch.

# Free Instagram post and story maker, no sign up

URL: https://opentempl.org/free-instagram-post-maker
Updated: 2026-11-02

Free Instagram post maker

Make Instagram posts, stories and carousels in OpenTempl without an account or a watermark. Start from a template or a blank 4:5 post, 1:1 square or 9:16 story, and export a PNG or JPG at full size.

 Sizes 
  Post, 4:5 portrait, 1080 by 1350 pixels  Square post, 1:1, 1080 by 1080  Story and reel cover, 9:16, 1080 by 1920  
 Instagram changes what it supports, so check its current specs. Magic resize turns a finished post into a story, or the other way round, in place or as a copy. 
 Make a post 
  Pick a size and a style. Soft and quiet:  soft pastel ,  Nordic minimal ,  quiet luxury . Loud:  Y2K chrome ,  maximal pop ,  aura .  Swap the words and the photo. Remove a background if the subject should sit on colour.  Save your colours, fonts and logo as a brand kit so every post matches.  Export a PNG or JPG.  
 Carousels and series 
 A carousel is a design with several pages. Export a ZIP of all pages and upload them in order. For a series, such as one card per product, use bulk create: paste a table and get a page for every row. 
 What it does not do 
 OpenTempl does not schedule or publish to Instagram. You export the image and post it yourself. 
 Pictures made with AI 
 The  prompt gallery  has copy and paste ChatGPT prompts for posts in 32 styles. The Generate tab in OpenTempl uses the same styles with your own OpenAI key.   Open the editor  

What size is an Instagram post?
A 4:5 portrait post is 1080 by 1350 pixels and a square post is 1080 by 1080. Check Instagram's current guidance, because it changes.

Can I make a carousel?
Yes. Add pages to a design and export a ZIP of all pages.

Can I schedule posts?
No. OpenTempl makes the image; you post it.

Is there a watermark?
No.

# Free menu maker: restaurant and cafe menu templates

URL: https://opentempl.org/free-menu-maker
Updated: 2026-11-02

Free menu maker

Design a menu, a cafe board or a recipe card in OpenTempl and export a print ready PDF with bleed and crop marks. No account, no watermark, and it works offline.

 Start from a menu 
 The  menus and food templates  cover cafe boards, restaurant menus and recipe cards. Other styles work for a menu too:  quiet luxury  for a dinner,  Nordic minimal  for a coffee bar,  seventies  for a diner. 
 Make it yours 
  Pick a template and a page size. A4 and A5 are common; type your own for a tall board.  Edit the dishes and prices. Paste a table from a spreadsheet to build a chart or a list, or use bulk create for one page per item, such as a table card per dish.  Set your brand colours and fonts with a brand kit.  Add a QR code that links to your site or an online menu.  Export the print PDF with bleed and crop marks, or a PNG for a screen.  
 What it does not do 
 OpenTempl is a design tool. It does not host a QR menu for you, take orders or print. You export the file and take it to a print shop or your own printer. It works in RGB; ask your printer about CMYK.   Open the editor  

Can I add a QR code?
Yes. Add a QR code element and type the address it should open.

What size should a menu be?
Common sizes are A4, A5 and a tall DL card. Ask your printer which they prefer.

Can I print at a copy shop?
Yes. Export the print PDF with bleed and crop marks and take it in.

# Free poster maker: no watermark, no account

URL: https://opentempl.org/free-poster-maker
Updated: 2026-11-02

Free poster maker

Make a poster in OpenTempl without an account, without a watermark and without paying. Start from one of 337 templates in 34 styles, or from a blank A3, A4 or custom page, and export a PNG or a print PDF with bleed and crop marks.

 Make a poster in five steps 
  Open the editor and pick a size. A3 portrait is the usual poster; A4, square and landscape are there too, and you can type your own.  Choose a style.  Swiss grid  for order,  riso zine  for ink and grain,  Seoul and Tokyo  for dense colour,  brutalist  for blunt type. All 34 are on the  templates page .  Replace the words and the picture. Double click text to edit. Drop a photo onto a frame and drag inside it to crop. Remove a photo's background if you need to.  Check it. The design check flags text that does not stand out from what is behind it, text that is too small, photos that will print soft and anything that sits off the page.  Export. PNG for screens, PDF for print, SVG if you want to keep editing in a vector tool.  
 For print 
 Choose the print PDF and set the bleed. OpenTempl adds the extra edge and crop marks that print shops ask for. Photos need enough pixels for the size you print, and the design check tells you when one does not. OpenTempl works in RGB; it has no CMYK output yet, so if your printer requires CMYK, ask whether they convert for you. 
 What is included 
 No watermark. Transparent PNG up to 4x. SVG. 1,344 Google Fonts plus your own font files. Curved text and ten text effects. Charts, QR codes and 200,000 icons. Version history. All free. 
 Posters from an image prompt 
 If you want a picture made by an image model first, the  prompt gallery  has copy and paste prompts for ChatGPT in 32 styles, including  halftone ,  risograph  and  Y2K .   Open the editor  

Is there a watermark?
No.

What resolution can I export?
PNG up to 4x the page size. At A3 that is a large file. PDF keeps text and vectors sharp at any size.

Can I print it at a shop?
Yes. Export the print PDF with bleed and crop marks and take it in. Ask whether they need CMYK.

Can I use my own fonts?
Yes. Add any font file, and it works offline.

Does it work offline?
Yes, after it has loaded once. See what needs a connection.

# Free presentation maker that opens PowerPoint files

URL: https://opentempl.org/free-presentation-maker
Updated: 2026-11-02

Free presentation maker, offline and without an account

OpenTempl makes slides you design yourself, opens PowerPoint files, and presents them with speaker notes. It is free, it works offline and it needs no account. It is not an AI deck generator: you choose the layout and write the words.

 What you can do 
  Start from a slide template or a blank 16:9 page. Styles that suit decks:  corporate clean ,  dark tech ,  academic ,  Swiss grid .  Open a .pptx file. Text stays editable with its bold and coloured words. Shapes, pictures, backgrounds, theme colours, fonts and speaker notes come across.  Add charts from a pasted spreadsheet, tables, icons, photos and video clips.  Animate with page transitions and entrance animations.  Present full screen with autoplay, or with the presenter view and notes on a second screen.  Export PowerPoint with editable text, PDF, MP4 video or GIF.  
 What does not come across 
 Charts, tables and SmartArt in PowerPoint files are not imported yet. Fonts that are not available get a close match, for example Calibri comes in as Carlito. Check the slides after you open them. 
 Why use it offline 
 You can present from a laptop with no wifi, with the deck and its fonts already on the machine. Open it once while connected so the fonts you use are stored.   Open the editor  

Can I open a .pptx file?
Yes. Slides, text, shapes, pictures, backgrounds and notes open. Charts, tables and SmartArt do not yet.

Does it support speaker notes?
Yes, in the editor and in presenter view.

Can I present offline?
Yes, once the app has loaded and you have used the fonts at least once while online.

Does it write slides with AI?
No. The Generate tab makes images with your own OpenAI key; it does not write a deck.

# How to make a poster with ChatGPT: 5 steps and prompts

URL: https://opentempl.org/guides/make-a-poster-with-chatgpt
Updated: 2026-11-02

How to make a poster with ChatGPT

You can make a poster with ChatGPT's image creation in a few minutes. The picture comes out better, and the words come out more reliably, if you decide a few things first. This guide goes through them and links to copy and paste prompts.

 1. Write the words first 
 Decide the headline, one supporting line and the small details (date, place, price). Keep them short. Image models draw letters as pictures, so long text goes wrong more often than short text. Read your own words twice. A typo in your prompt is copied into the poster. 
 2. Pick a style 
 &quot;A poster for a gig&quot; gives you the same generic picture as everyone else. A named style gives you a point of view: a risograph print, a halftone duotone, a papercut, Y2K chrome. The  prompt gallery  has 32 styles, each with a sample, so you can see what you will get before you ask. 
 3. Paste a prompt and change three things 
 Open a style page, copy the prompt, and paste it into ChatGPT with image creation on. Change the subject, the words in quotes and, if you like, the colours. The prompts name the format, such as A3 portrait or a 4:5 post, so the layout fits. 
 4. Fix one thing at a time 
 If the result is close, ask for one change: &quot;make the dots coarser&quot;, &quot;move the headline lower&quot;, &quot;use a warmer red&quot;. Several changes at once make the model redo everything. 
 5. Check the words and finish 
 Read every letter. If a word is wrong, you can ask again, or you can use the picture as the background and set the words yourself. In  OpenTempl , the Generate tab with your own OpenAI key can leave empty room for the words, so you add them as live text and fix a typo in a second. 
 Before you print 
 Check the size and the resolution. A picture from an image model may be smaller than your print size. Leave room for the margin, and ask the printer about bleed. OpenTempl's print PDF adds bleed and crop marks; see the  poster maker . 
 Limits to know 
  Results vary, and the same prompt gives a different picture each time.  Free ChatGPT accounts have limits on image creation that change, so check your own account.  Exact placement is hard to control. Treat the image as artwork and place the text yourself when it matters.  Read OpenAI's current terms before you use an image commercially.  

Is it free to make a poster with ChatGPT?
It depends on your ChatGPT plan and its current limits for image creation. The prompts on this site and OpenTempl are free.

Why is the text on my poster wrong?
Image models draw letters as pictures and sometimes get them wrong. Use short words, put them in quotes and check the result, or add the words afterwards in an editor.

What size should I ask for?
Name the format in the prompt. A3 portrait suits a poster, 4:5 portrait suits an Instagram post and 9:16 suits a story.

Can I print the result?
Yes, if it has enough pixels for the print size. Check the resolution, and ask your printer about bleed.

Can I edit the poster afterwards?
Yes. Open the image in an editor such as OpenTempl and add or change the text, colours and layout.

# OpenTempl MCP server: let your assistant design

URL: https://opentempl.org/mcp
Updated: 2026-11-02

Let your assistant design in OpenTempl

OpenTempl has an MCP server. Connect it to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any other assistant that speaks MCP, ask for a poster, a post or a deck, and the assistant builds it in OpenTempl, looks at a preview of every version, fixes what is off and gives you a link. The link opens the design in the editor, where you can change anything and export it. Free, with no account and no key.

 Address 
  https://opentempl.org/api/mcp  
 Connect 
     Where  How      Claude (web and desktop)  Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector. Name it OpenTempl and paste the address.    ChatGPT  Settings, Apps, Advanced settings: turn on developer mode, then create an app with the address.    Claude Code   claude mcp add --transport http opentempl https://opentempl.org/api/mcp     Cursor  In  ~/.cursor/mcp.json :  {&quot;mcpServers&quot;: {&quot;opentempl&quot;: {&quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://opentempl.org/api/mcp&quot;}}}     VS Code  In  .vscode/mcp.json :  {&quot;servers&quot;: {&quot;opentempl&quot;: {&quot;type&quot;: &quot;http&quot;, &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://opentempl.org/api/mcp&quot;}}}     Anything else  Any client with Streamable HTTP. For clients that only run local servers:  npx mcp-remote https://opentempl.org/api/mcp      
 Then ask for something, for example: &quot;Make a poster for our jazz night on Friday 14 November at Kafé Lyktan, 20:00, free entry. Dark, warm, a bit of brass.&quot; 
 What the assistant can do 
  Search the 337 templates by purpose, mood, style and size, and look at them.  Start from a template and replace the words, photos and colours, or build a design from a blank page.  Use every part of the editor: text with any Google Font, effects and curves, shapes and custom vector paths, gradients and patterns, lines and arrows, photo frames with masks, filters and duotone, icons from 200,000, the OpenTempl art library, charts, tables, QR codes, pages, speaker notes, transitions and animation.  Search free Unsplash photos, with the photographer credited.  See a rendered preview after every change, drawn by the same code the editor exports with, so it can check its own work.  Hand you a link. Opening it makes an ordinary design on your computer.  
 Tools 
     Tool  What it does      design_guide  The handbook: every edit and property, and the rules for professional layouts.    search_templates, get_template  Find templates and read exactly how they are built.    list_styles, list_formats, list_library  The 34 template styles with their fonts and palettes, every size, and the art library.    create_design, edit_design, undo_edits  Make and refine a design. Every call returns a preview.    get_design, preview_design  Read a design's elements and render any page.    search_photos, search_icons, search_fonts  Photos from Unsplash, open source icons and Google Fonts.     
 Privacy 
 What the assistant sends to make a design (the words, colours and photo links) is kept on OpenTempl's server so the link can open it, and deleted 90 days after the last change. It holds nothing about you: no account, no name, no address. Once you open the link, the design is a copy on your computer, and what you do with it stays there, the same as any other design in OpenTempl. 

Does it cost anything?
No. The server, the templates, the previews and the editor are free. Previews come from a shared free allowance; on a very busy day an assistant may get the link without a preview.

Which assistant works best?
One that can look at images, because it checks every preview. Recent Claude and ChatGPT models both handle it well.

Can it edit a design I made myself?
Not yet. The assistant works on designs it starts. Once you open its link, the design is yours to edit in the app like any other.

Is the server open source?
Yes. It is in the OpenTempl repository, under the MIT license, like the rest of OpenTempl.

---

# Open source Canva alternative: OpenTempl (MIT)

URL: https://opentempl.org/open-source-canva
Updated: 2026-11-02

Is there an open source version of Canva?

Canva is not open source. A few open source projects cover part of what it does, and OpenTempl covers the part most people mean: designing posters, social posts, slides, menus and invitations from templates.

 OpenTempl is MIT licensed, works offline, needs no account and has 337 templates in 34 styles. It is not affiliated with Canva. 
 What open source means here 
 MIT licensed.  Source code on GitHub . The MIT licence lets you use OpenTempl for any purpose, read how it works, change it, share your changes and ship your own version. 
 Two kinds of files inside the app carry their own terms. The photos, voxel objects, characters and textures in the built in library were made for OpenTempl and are free to use for anything. Icons from Iconify and photos from Openverse keep the licences they came with. 
 Open source tools that replace parts of Canva 
     Tool  Licence  Best for  Templates  Offline      OpenTempl  MIT  Posters, social posts, slides, menus, invitations  337 in 34 styles  Yes    Penpot  MPL 2.0  Interface design and prototyping with developers  Libraries, not poster templates  Self hosted, or in the browser    Doory  Open source  A self hosted design editor with live editing  Basic  Self hosted    HyCanvas  AGPL 3.0  A self hostable editor with your own AI key  Basic  Self hosted    Inkscape  GPL  Vector illustration and logos  Few  Yes    GIMP  GPL  Photo editing  No  Yes    Graphite  Open source  Node based vector and raster art  No  Runs in the browser     
 Read from each project's own page and from directory listings in November 2026. Licences, features and activity change, so look at the repositories before you decide. Doory and HyCanvas are young projects. 
 Penpot is the one most lists name first. It is a good tool, built for teams who design apps and websites, closer to Figma than to Canva. If you want to lay out an event poster in ten minutes, OpenTempl is closer to what you wanted. 
 Run it yourself 
  git clone https://github.com/noah-thing/opentempl
cd opentempl
npm install
npm run dev  
 The editor opens on a local address.  npm run build  writes the static site, and the  apps/desktop  folder packages it as an Electron app. 
 There is no OpenTempl server to host. The web version is static files, and live sessions between people go directly from browser to browser. 
 Help build it 
 Open items today include PowerPoint import of charts, tables and SmartArt, kerning and ligature controls, CMYK aware print PDFs, a plugin API, code signed installers and an optional self hosted sync server. Open an issue or send a fix at  the repository . 
 Limits 
 OpenTempl is at version 0.1 and has one maintainer. It has no team workspaces, no phone app, no cloud sync and a library of 337 templates. If you need those, use a hosted tool.   Open the editor  

Is Canva open source?
No. Canva is proprietary software.

Is there an open source version of Canva?
There is no official one. OpenTempl is an independent open source design app for the same kind of work. Penpot is an open source design tool aimed at product teams.

What licence does OpenTempl use?
The MIT licence. Library photos, objects and textures made for OpenTempl are free for any use. Iconify icons and Openverse photos keep their own licences.

Can I self host OpenTempl?
The web app is static files, so you can serve it from any web server. There is no OpenTempl backend to run. A self hosted sync server for several devices is a future item, not a feature today.

Does OpenTempl collect my data?
There are no accounts and no OpenTempl server that stores your designs. Fonts load from Google Fonts, and live sessions use a signalling service so two computers can find each other. The facts page lists what needs a connection.

Is this the same as OpenTemplate.org or other projects with similar names?
No. OpenTempl is a design app. It is unrelated to template engines such as Total.js OpenTemplates or the OpenOffice template site OpenTemplate.org.

# ChatGPT poster prompts: 31 styles to copy

URL: https://opentempl.org/prompts
Updated: 2026-11-02

ChatGPT poster prompts

Pick a style, copy the prompt, paste it into ChatGPT. Every style has a sample image, its palette, three versions for common jobs (a gig poster, an Instagram post, a menu) and notes on what to change. 31 styles so far.

     Bold Flat Colour  Fat red shapes on emerald, yellow type stacked tight, a Seoul canteen poster.       Halftone Duotone  A photographed face or animal in two clashing inks, giant type biting into it.       Pixel World  Voxel flowers, dither clouds and chunky dot type float in a cut paper sky.       Grain Shape Animals  Blocky animals built from clean shapes, sprayed with soft grain on warm yellow.       Brush Marker Lettering  Fat pink letters painted with a loaded brush, outlined in electric blue.       Riso Market Scene  Overlapping ink people carry baskets through a market in pink, yellow and teal.       Club Flyer Print  One blue ink on cream, a DJ inside a globe, old school flyer type.       Folk Cutout Garden  Hand cut flowers, horses and birds mirrored on black, bright as embroidered cloth.       Inflatable Type  Puffy letters and balloon animals, taut and glossy, with colour pooling in the folds.       Stitched Pixel Type  Letters and flowers woven from tiny squares, like a sampler stitched on a screen.       Grain Glow Type  Warped, blurred letters glow like heat, wrapped in coarse grain and one hot colour.       Acid Black Wire  Black, white and one acid green, with chrome and mono type on a grid.       Extruded Block Letters  Giant solid letters as buildings, extruded in flat colour with a clean sunny shadow.       Sticker Cartoon Pop  Fat outlined cartoon props float on a blue grid, each with a sticker shadow.       Blob Gradient Pop  Soft fluid blobs in blue, pink and orange swirl behind rounded letters.       Sliced Portrait Cover  A studio face cut into shifting strips under a refined serif masthead.       Pop Cutout Collage  A hard cut figure on a red starburst, with tape, tulips and bright paper.       Psychedelic Lettering  Letters melt into ribbons around a halftone portrait, printed in two hot inks.       Sunny Travel Poster  Flat cut shapes, palm silhouettes and a bright cream border, a postcard from 1958.       Riso Two Ink  A photo split into red and blue ink, grainy and not quite aligned.       Oil Pastel Scribble  A homey scene drawn in waxy crayon on white paper, creases and all.       Blue Ink Doodle  Crowded biro doodles in cobalt, with plain red grotesk giant over the top.       Flash Editorial Photo  Direct flash, wet skin, saturated sky and stickers slapped on like a zine.       Blob Mascot  A giant blob with huge eyes looms over tiny angry friends, flat and funny.       Holographic Y2K  Chrome blobs, a rainbow disc and glass windows, a dream of a 2001 desktop.       Keycap Type  Words spelled on chunky keyboard keys, tilted in isometric rows on pure black.       Athlete Giant Type  One athlete cut out in front of a word as tall as the wall.       Liquid Chrome Type  Letters melted into mirror metal, blobby and bright, framed by a thin HUD border.       Layered Papercut  Stacked paper layers form a glowing valley, lit from below like a tiny theatre.       Cutout Plant Collage  Cut out real leaves beside tall serif letters, with one wild red leaf.       Neon Tube Glow  Thin tubes of cold blue light trace logos on black, humming and slightly smeared.     How to make a poster with ChatGPT 
 Decide the words first and keep them short. Pick a style so the picture has a point of view. Paste the prompt, change the subject and the words, and send it. Ask for one change at a time. Check every word before you save the file. The  full guide  goes through it step by step. 
 How these prompts are built 
 Each prompt names a medium, a palette with colour values, a composition, a texture, the exact words to draw and a list of things to keep out. Specific prompts give you more of what you meant. They come from the same written art directions that OpenTempl's Generate tab uses, one for each style. 
 About the words on the poster 
 Image models sometimes misspell. Every prompt here includes your words in quotes, and each page tells you to read the result. If you want to fix a word without making the picture again, OpenTempl can leave room for the words and set them as live text on top of the image. 
 Make it in OpenTempl 
 OpenTempl is a free, open source design app that works offline and needs no account. Its Generate tab uses these styles with your own OpenAI key. OpenAI charges you for the images you make, and OpenTempl takes nothing.   Open the Generate tab  

What is the best ChatGPT prompt for a poster?
One that names the style, the colours, the layout and the exact words. The prompts on these pages do all four, and they leave room to change the subject and the text.

Why does ChatGPT misspell my poster text?
Image models draw letters as pictures, and they sometimes get them wrong. Keep the words short, put them in quotes and check the result. In OpenTempl you can add the words as live text instead.

Can I use the images commercially?
That depends on the terms of the service that made the image. Read OpenAI's current terms before you use an image for work.

Do the prompts work in Gemini or Midjourney?
They are plain text, so you can try them there. Results differ from tool to tool.

Is it free?
The prompts and OpenTempl are free. Making images costs whatever your AI account charges.

Updated: 2026-11-02

A bold flat colour poster prompt for ChatGPT

A flat colour illustration built from a few huge shapes in saturated inks, printed as a poster with perfect hard edges and tiny cut out details in cream. It looks like a designer cut the shapes by hand and sent them to a good screen printer.

Signature: objects cropped by the edges at diagonals; tiny scale patterns cut into the hero shapes; dots and bowls as punctuation; type overlapping the artwork; ground colour reused for small info text

# OpenTempl facts: licence, features and limits

URL: https://opentempl.org/facts
Updated: 2026-11-02

OpenTempl facts

OpenTempl is a free, open source (MIT) design app for posters, social media posts and slides, with 337 templates, that works offline and needs no account. This page lists what can be checked, with the date. Last updated November 2026.

 Identity 
  Name: OpenTempl. Written as one word, capital O and T. Also called the free open source Canva alternative.  Maker: Noah, in Stockholm. Independent project.  Made by Noah on X .  Website: https://opentempl.org  Licence: MIT. Source code: https://github.com/noah-thing/opentempl.  Price: free. No paid plan, no trial, no ads.  Not affiliated with Canva or OpenAI.  
 Counts 
  Templates: 337, in 34 styles and 33 kinds of document.  Styles for image generation (Looks): 32.  Fonts: 1,344 Google Fonts plus your own font files.  Shapes: 23. Icons: about 200,000 through Iconify.  
 Where it runs 
  In a web browser at https://opentempl.org. Chrome and Edge may offer to install it as an app.  Desktop builds for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux are made with Electron. They are on the  download page .  No phone app.  
 Formats 
  Import: PDF with editable text, PowerPoint (text, shapes, pictures, backgrounds, speaker notes), the OpenTempl file. Charts, tables and SmartArt in PowerPoint files are not imported yet.  Export: PNG (transparent, up to 4x), JPG, WebP, SVG, PDF for screen or print with bleed and crop marks, PowerPoint with editable text, MP4, GIF, a ZIP of pages, the editable OpenTempl file.  Colour: RGB. No CMYK output or ICC profiles yet.  
 Offline and the internet 
  The app opens and edits without a connection after it has loaded once. New designs can be made offline.  Designs are saved on your device, in the browser or the desktop app. There is no OpenTempl account and no OpenTempl server that stores your designs.  Needs a connection: the first load, Google Fonts you have not used before (they are cached after first use), icon search, stock photo search (Openverse), the first use of background removal (it downloads a model once), live sessions with other people, and the Generate tab.  Fonts load from Google Fonts. The static pages on this site load no third party fonts or scripts.  Live sessions go directly between browsers and are encrypted with a key in the link. A signalling service helps the two computers find each other.  Generate: you paste your own OpenAI key. It is kept on your device and your prompt goes to OpenAI. OpenAI bills your account. OpenTempl charges nothing.  
 What it does not do 
  No team workspaces, approvals or brand controls at company scale.  No cloud sync between devices. Move the file yourself.  No phone app.  No scheduling or publishing to social networks.  No CMYK output.  A library of 337 templates, not millions.  Version 0.1. One maintainer. Desktop installers are not code signed yet.  
 Not the same as 
 OpenTempl is a design app. It is unrelated to the Total.js OpenTemplates engine, the OpenTemplate PHP engine, or OpenTemplate.org, the OpenOffice template site. 

---

# What is OpenTempl? Free open source design app

URL: https://opentempl.org/about
Updated: 2026-11-02

What is OpenTempl

OpenTempl is a free, open source (MIT) design app for posters, social media posts and slides, with 337 templates, that works offline and needs no account.

 It makes posters, Instagram posts and stories, slides, menus, flyers, invitations and business cards. You start from one of 337 templates or a blank page, drag things where you want them, and export when it looks right. It opens PowerPoint and PDF files, and it exports PNG, SVG, PDF, PowerPoint, MP4 and GIF. 
 Why it exists 
 Noah wanted a design tool he could open on a train without logging in, one that left him with files he owns and did not hold exports behind a plan. So he built one. It is a separate editor written from scratch, with its own templates, its own look and its own renderer. It is not a copy of Canva and it uses nothing from Canva. 
 What makes it different 
  It works offline and creates new designs offline.  There is no account to make and no paid tier.  337 templates in 34 styles, each drawn as its own world: Swiss grid, riso zine, brutalist, Bauhaus, Seoul and Tokyo event posters, pixel art, Y2K chrome and more.  The exports other tools keep behind a paid plan are included: transparent PNG, SVG, print PDF with bleed and crop marks.  It is MIT licensed.  
 Who makes it 
 OpenTempl is made by  Noah , in Stockholm. It is a one person project. Feedback and bug reports go to the repository once it is open, or to Noah on X. 
 What comes next 
 PowerPoint import of charts, tables and SmartArt. Kerning and ligature controls. CMYK aware print PDFs. A plugin API. Code signed installers. An optional self hosted sync server for people who want designs on several devices. These are plans, not promises with dates. 
 The name 
 OpenTempl is short for open templates. The app is unrelated to other projects with similar names, such as the Total.js OpenTemplates engine or OpenTemplate.org. 
 See also:  the facts page ,  how OpenTempl compares with Canva  and  the prompt gallery . 

---

# Download OpenTempl: web app and desktop builds

URL: https://opentempl.org/download
Updated: 2026-11-02

Use OpenTempl

OpenTempl runs in your browser and works offline once it has loaded. The desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux is the same editor in its own window.

 Web app 
 Open https://opentempl.org. Chrome and Edge may offer to install it as an app, which then opens without a browser window. Your designs are saved on your device. Clear the site data and they go with it, so save a file for anything you want to keep. 
 Desktop app 
 Version 0.1.0. Every build is listed with its checksum on the  release page . 
   macOS, Apple silicon  (M1 and newer)   macOS, Intel    Windows 10 and 11    Linux, AppImage  or  .deb   
 The first builds are not code signed. On macOS, right click the app and choose Open the first time. On Windows, choose More info, then Run anyway. 
 System 
 A recent version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari for the web app. Designs with many large photos use a lot of memory; close other heavy tabs for big posters. Background removal downloads a small model the first time you use it.   Open the editor  

Is it free?
Yes. There is no paid plan, trial or watermark. The licence is MIT.

Do I need an account?
No.

Does it work offline?
Yes, after it has loaded once. Fonts you have not used before, icon search, stock photos and live sessions need a connection. See the offline page.

Where are my files?
On your device. Export the editable OpenTempl file to keep a copy or move a design to another computer.
